intent.text: ses moves: the vsect maturation plan gets one independent reviewer who did not author it, ideally from a different model family, with the review's findings recorded before the plan is adopted. Reasons: the estate's own numbers say the decisive property is independence from the author, not headcount. Independent checkers found defects in about 43% of landings; self-checks confirmed 116 of 116. A council of Claude seats shares training and framing, so five agreeing seats can still share one blind spot; a single reviewer from another family is a different error source. A council is still useful after that for contested judgment calls the reviewer flags, since those need deliberation rather than a second check. So: (1) one out-of-family independent review as the gate; (2) any finding the author disputes goes to the council as a question; (3) the reviewer's sign-off and the council's record both go in the plan's history. Caveat: this is a recommendation, not a measurement. Whether a different family actually catches more than a same-family fresh session is not established here; the 43% figure compares independent checkers to self-checks, not one family to another.
